The petitioner seeks to quash the impugned private complaint in old C.C.No.5 of 2016 and new C.C.No.1166 of 2023 on the file of the learned Judicial Magistrate No.V, Tirunelveli, registered for the offences under Sections 406, 420 and 506 of IPC.

2. The allegations in the complaint is that the respondent was made to believe that the patta in respect of the disputed property was transferred in her name and the document was registered; that the petitioners along with the other accused had obtained her signature in the sale deed dated 31.03.2008 bearing Document No.543 of 2008 in the office of the Sub Registrar; that she had not received any sale consideration; and that the complaint given by her was referred as mistake of fact and hence she was constrained to file a private complaint.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the allegations are false; that the respondent had filed a suit to declare that the disputed property belongs to her and also for a declaration that the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 05/01/2026 11:35:27 am ) sale deed is null and void in O.S.No.99 of 2014 on the file of the Principal Subordinate Judge, Tirunelveli that the said suit was dismissed; that an appeal was filed in A.S.No.08 of 2020 on the file of the First Additional District Judge, Tirunelveli and the same was dismissed on 09.09.2022; that the co-accused was also discharged by the trial Court; that the complaint given by the respondent to the police was closed as it did not disclose any of the offences; and that the impugned complaint is an abuse of process of law and is liable to be quashed.

4. Though notice has been served on the respondent and her name has been printed in the cause list,
none has entered appearance on her behalf.
Hence, this Court appointed Mr.K.Pragadesh Ganapathy, as a legal aid counsel to represent the respondent.

5. As stated above, it is the case of the respondent that the petitioners in the guise of transferring the patta in her name had obtained signature in a sale deed dated 31.03.2008 bearing Document No.543 of 2008 in the office of the Sub Registrar; that later she came to know that a sale deed was executed in favour of third parties; that she had not https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 05/01/2026 11:35:27 am ) received any sale consideration; and that she had lodged a complaint before the police, which was referred as 'mistake of fact' and hence, she filed the private complaint.
6.

The learned legal aid counsel appearing for the respondent would submit that the findings of the Civil Court would not be binding in a criminal case; that the co-accused was discharged, since there was no allegation against him; that allegations are only against the petitioners and that the points raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners cannot be adjudicated in a quash petition and sought for dismissal of the quash petition.

7. It is seen from the record that challenging the sale deed in which it is alleged that the respondent's signature was obtained by the petitioners by playing fraud, the respondent had filed a suit in OS No.191 of 2020 before the Principal Sub Court, Tirunelveli, for a declaration that the sale deed is a null and void.
The said suit was dismissed and the appeal filed by the respondent in AS No.8 of 2020 before the Principal District Judge, Tirunelveli also came to be dismissed on 09.09.2022.

The https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 05/01/2026 11:35:27 am ) allegations made in the R.Kannadasan vs M.Madathi @ Esther on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23134125/
2 impugned complaint are the same as the averments in the above civil proceedings initiated by the respondent.
The respondent's version has been disbelieved by the trial Court and the appellate Court.
8. That apart, it is seen that based on the complaint given by the respondent, the police conducted an investigation.

The police found that the signature found in the sale deed was not forged; that the petitioners and the respondent are closely related to each other and that the investigation revealed that the respondent had in fact received the sale consideration and closed the case as action dropped.
9.

In the light of the findings of the civil Court which pertains to the very same allegations made in the impugned complaint and the report of the police that the respondent had infact received sale consideration, this Court is of the view that the impugned complaint is an abuse of process of law.
Hence, the impugned complaint is liable to be quashed.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

10. Accordingly, the impugned proceedings in old C.C.No.5 of 2016 and new C.C.No.1166 of 2023 on the file of the learned Judicial Magistrate No.V, Tirunelveli, is quashed and this Criminal Original Petition is allowed.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
11. The Legal Services Authority shall pay the scheduled fee to Mr.K.Pragadesh Ganapathy, the learned Legal Aid Counsel for the respondent.
